Learning experience design · Case study

A road safety animation that teaches learners to investigate, not guess

I designed a learner avatar and a 9-panel animated storyboard that shows new Roads Technicians how to investigate a safety concern step by step.

Learner-centred designStorytellingVyond animationCharacter systemAI-assisted workflow
Role

Solo: analysis, character, storyboard

Timeline

4 days

Output

Avatar, 6 poses, 9 panels, motion test

Tools

Vyond, Figma, Procreate, InDesign

Client and scenario details are anonymized.

01

The problem

Scenario

A curved road has repeated night-time run-off-road collisions, and the municipality needs a defensible case file.

Learner problem

New Roads Technicians may submit incomplete findings or jump to early assumptions.

Learning solution

A short animation that models a structured investigation, from case history to supervisor review.

02

Learner and objectives

Empathy map: what the learner needs

Too much informationRisk of jumping to conclusionsUnclear documentation Step-by-step processVisual observation cuesCase file structureReview checkpoint

Show the investigation process, not a reconstruction of the accident.

Learning objectives

Identify

Review the concern and case history for patterns.

Observe

Compare day and night, walking and driver views, signs and lines.

Document

Record observations and stakeholder input clearly.

Prepare

Organize findings before final recommendations.

03

Character and pose system

Alex is a learner avatar, not an expert who gives answers. Six reusable poses keep him active across every scene and make new scenes quick to build.

04

Storyboard

Select a panel to enlarge
Panels 1–3

From assignment to investigation plan

01Receive the assignmentIdentify the investigation focus.

02Review the case historyLook for repeated patterns in reports and records.

03Plan the investigation anglesPlan multiple observation angles before going on site.

Panels 4–6

Multi-angle observation

04Day and night observationCompare the same site in different conditions.

05Walking vs driver perspectiveDifferent views reveal different details.

06Check signs and linesReview warning signs, markings and edge lines.

Panels 7–9

From evidence to review

07Gather and document evidenceRecord notes and stakeholder input.

08Organize findingsBuild a structured case file.

09Present for reviewGet review before any recommendation.

05

Design rationale

Learner-centred storytelling

Built around Alex's process, not the accident.

Structured flow

Briefing → history → plan → observe → evidence → organize → review.

Brand-aligned visuals

Restrained layout and clear hierarchy, following the client's brand standards.

Key iteration: on Day 2 the draft drifted toward the case file and the accident, so I reframed every panel around Alex's thinking. AI use: AI supported research and wording; I compared suggestions, questioned assumptions and made the final decisions myself.
